thread:
Maria L: quick q — for v2 API we're cleaning up error semantics. today some validation/param issues come back as 500. can we decide on a small, consistent mapping?
Aj Patel: yes — agree we should standardize. which codes are we thinking (400 vs 422 vs 409)? also need to consider SDKs that inspect codes.
Ryan K: my proposal: 400 = syntactic / missing required (JSON parse, bad types), 422 = semantic/validation (e.g. "max_tokens" too large for model), 409 = conflict (duplicate or state mismatch), 429 = rate limit, 503/504 = transient infra/retryable, 500 = unexpected/unhandled. keep 5xx for retryable infra or true server crashes.
Sophia T: heads-up: some customer logic currently retries on 500; we should avoid turning transient-retryable errors into 4xx. also would be nice to include an explicit "retryable" boolean in the body for clients that don't want to guess. :thinking:
Kevin M: +1 to the body flag. Also suggest an "error_code" machine string (e.g., "invalid_input", "rate_limited") and an "error_class" namespace for programmatic matching — SDKs can use that rather than raw HTTP code.
Maria L: example payload suggestion:
```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "embedding dimension 1536 incompatible with model redwood-embed-1 (2048 expected)",
    "error_code": "invalid_embedding_size",
    "error_class": "input.validation",
    "retryable": false,
    "docs_url": "https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#invalid_embedding_size"
  }
}
```
Aj Patel: that looks good. for backward compat, propose a header to opt into strict semantics so we can roll gradually: `X-Redwood-Error-Mode: legacy | strict`. legacy keeps old behavior (some validation -> 500), strict enforces the new codes. default to legacy for 4 weeks then reevaluate.
infra-bot: Deploy coordinator: note — need a canary path for header rollout and monitoring hooks for error shape changes.
Ryan K: small pushback: defaulting to legacy means we maintain both codepaths longer. prefer opt-in strict (customers set header) for 4 weeks, then flip default. avoids surprise.
Sophia T: compromise: default legacy but support `Prefer: strict-errors=1` and a feature flag per org. document heavily and add a migration guide.
Maria L: agreed. decision: implement strict mode behind header `X-Redwood-Error-Mode` + `Prefer` hint; default legacy for initial rollout, use canary customers with strict. once stable flip default after metrics look good (target: 8 weeks). Action items: open PR for runtime + schema changes, add error class/fields to error schema, add SDK tests, update changelog and docs, run canary. I'll open PR and ticket. tagging reviewers: @Aj Patel @Ryan K @Kevin M. PR #8345 (draft).
Aj Patel: I'll review PR today. :thumbsup:
Kevin M: I'll add unit + integration tests for python + node SDKs to assert both header shapes and legacy fallback.
Maria L: added TODO to ticket 1921 and console doc item for per-route error display.
deploy-bot: Recommend: canary rollout 10% of traffic -> monitor 5xx/4xx ratios and SDK error parsers for failures.
Maria L: perfect. thanks all — I'll post a short announcement in #announcements when PR is merged and schedule a sync with support for customer questions.
